segments.text: People in old photos didn't smile because they had to hold still for minutes. Not really.
Within a few years, the wait dropped to just seconds, and the faces stayed serious.
The real reason was manners. Back then, a big toothy grin looked silly, even drunk. Proper people kept their mouths small.
So in London, photographer Richard Beard told his sitters to say prunes, for a neat, tight little mouth.
Then cameras got cheap. Kodak's one dollar Brownie, in {1900,|nineteen hundred,} turned photos into fun snapshots, and the ads were full of happy faces.
In {1943,|nineteen forty three,} a Texas newspaper quoted former ambassador Joseph Davies with his trick. Just say cheese. It's an automatic smile.
The ch pulls your lips apart, and the long ee stretches them wide. Try it right now.
So the word didn't make us smile. Cameras did. Follow for a weird everyday truth daily.
